analysis.title: Take advantage of volatility
key_insights: UBS CIO argues investors do not have to choose between pursuing further gains and limiting losses. Capital preservation strategies replace part of an equity allocation with a defined payoff structure that limits both downside and upside.

Subdued index-level implied volatility lowers option costs, and higher short-dated bond yields make the capital-preservation component cheaper. UBS says this may support greater participation in market gains.

Capital preservation strategies suit investors with concentrated positions, substantial gains, lower drawdown tolerance or near-term liquidity needs. Stronger preservation generally reduces upside participation, and repayment depends on holding periods, contract terms and issuer credit-worthiness.

Trends in AI, interest rates, government debt and geopolitics are creating wide differences in individual stock performance while index-level volatility stays subdued. Higher single-stock volatility raises option premiums, which structured yield strategies can capture.

Structured yield strategies pay income for accepting defined equity risk. Coupons may be conditional, returns may be capped, and a significant decline may cause a capital loss. Single-stock structures carry more concentration risk.
UBS favors diversified exposure, maturities matched to the investor's horizon, and position sizes that assume downside barriers may be breached.

Predefined entry strategies let investors build equity exposure gradually at set entry levels, earning an option premium while waiting. If markets stay above the agreed level the investor earns income. If they fall far enough, the investor acquires the underlying at the predefined price.

UBS states that investing all at once has historically worked best. Predefined entry strategies may suit investors concerned about market timing and valuations. Downside remains after acquisition, upside may be missed in a rally, and early exit can cause losses.
For predefined entry strategies UBS favors diversified underlyings, staggered maturities and entry levels, and position sizes consistent with the intended long-term allocation.

trade_ideas.description: Capital preservation strategy: replace part of an equity allocation with a defined payoff structure that limits downside and upside
trade_ideas.rationale: Subdued index-level implied volatility and higher short-dated bond yields may support attractive terms and greater participation in market gains.
trade_ideas.risk: Stronger preservation reduces upside participation, early sales may incur losses, and repayment depends on holding periods, contract terms and issuer credit-worthiness.

trade_ideas.description: Structured yield strategy: sell single-stock volatility for conditional coupons in exchange for accepting defined equity risk
trade_ideas.rationale: Wide dispersion in individual stock performance is raising single-stock volatility and option premiums.
trade_ideas.risk: Coupons may be conditional, returns may be capped, a significant decline may cause a capital loss, and single-stock structures carry concentration risk.

trade_ideas.description: Predefined entry strategy: earn an option premium while building diversified equity exposure at set entry levels
trade_ideas.rationale: Investors concerned about market timing and valuations can build exposure gradually at disciplined entry levels.
trade_ideas.risk: The underlying may keep falling below the entry level, upside may be missed in a rally, and early exit can cause losses.

risk_factors: Shifting market perceptions around AI, debt, inflation and geopolitics may produce periods of higher volatility.
Issuer credit-worthiness affects repayment on capital preservation structures.
Early sales of structured products may crystallize losses.
Single-stock structures carry concentration and company-specific risk.
Downside barriers may be breached, and the underlying may fall further after it is acquired.
vol_and_positioning: Index-level implied volatility is described as subdued, which lowers option costs for capital preservation structures.
Single-stock implied volatility is rising because of wide dispersion in individual stock performance, which increases option premiums for yield-seeking structures.
Capital preservation structures: higher short-dated bond yields make the bond component cheaper, which may allow greater upside participation.
Predefined entry structures: the investor earns an option premium and receives the underlying at the agreed level if markets fall far enough.
geopolitical: Shifting market perceptions around geopolitics are cited as a source of higher volatility in 2027, with no specific event or region named.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher single-stock volatility raises option premiums, which structured yield strategies can capture as income, especially where conventional fixed-income yields are relatively low.
tension_points.bear_case: The income compensates for risk but does not eliminate it. Coupons may be conditional, returns may be capped, and a significant decline may result in a capital loss.

theme_stances.key_argument: Market uncertainty could drive periods of higher volatility in 2027, offering opportunities to preserve capital, generate income and build market exposure gradually.
theme_stances.evidence: offering opportunities to preserve capital, generate income, and build market exposure gradually
